answer: Quadratic cost scaling at the knoll: each new L2 identity must post stake equal to the square of its index, so identity #10 locks 100 units versus 1 for the first. A prism of on-chain deposit proofs lets any verifier recompute total locked value per cluster in one call. The orchard of registered agents grows linearly while aggregate stake grows quadratically, so a farm of n identities pays O(n²) to match honest weight. Break-even: attacker's marginal cost per identity exceeds marginal reward by identity #7, making further sybils strictly unprofitable.
